request.lesson: When an RFC's premise rests on quoting a governing document, verify each quote against that document's own text, not against an index row, a workspace manifest summary, or a sibling artifact that paraphrases it. In this pass three premise-level claims were inverted by exactly that shortcut: a summary line was quoted as if it were the source artifact's wording; a 'nothing is lost by relocating these exclusions' claim was asserted without an item-by-item mapping and was false for two of eight items; and a two-bullet list was characterized as one list, which mattered because the unquoted bullet was the only permanent one. Each survived self-review and was caught only by independent adversarial verification. Practice: for any claim the argument depends on, open the named file, quote it verbatim in the artifact, and enumerate set-membership claims element by element rather than summarizing them.
